# Handoff: avra-lane-ui-language (the ctx lane)

## Lane and scope
The `ctx` language feature (context values, set by a line, read as `ctx.name`), built in steps:
1 the frame and its rows; 2 the survey and laws (`ctx.required`, `ctx.unread` warning);
3a capture (a lambda runs under the frame it was made under); 3b A2 (a `@placed` trait's boxes

# ctx step 3 — capture: the mechanism, for a ruling before it's built

The design (H2, F1–F3) says what is captured. This note is how, because it changes every closure's box
and costs something on every closure call.

## The frame rides in the closure box, at slot 1
- A box is today `[code, lanes…]`; it becomes `[code, frame, lanes…]`. The frame is managed (the box
  holds a reference), and it is NULL where nothing is set. The slot can't trail the lanes: a body
  learns its lanes as it lowers, and its entry needs the frame's slot first.
- A lambda with no captures is today a static box (`[code]`, no allocation). It stays static while no
  frame is set. Where one is set at its making, a new row `avra_fn_framed(static)` makes
  `[code, frame]`. A program that never sets a context pays nothing at a making.
- A lifted body's entry reads slot 1 when the box is longer than one slot. It calls a new row
  `avra_ctx_enter(frame) -> int`:
  - when the frame is already current (the common case: both NULL, or the same frame), it changes
    nothing and answers 0;
  - otherwise it pushes a frame holding the made frame's pairs over the caller's (prev = the caller's
    frame) and answers 1, so the step-1 back restores the caller's frame by every way out.
  - The body's scope ends with `back` only where the answer was 1.
- **Cost per closure call, no contexts:** one length test, one load, one call that compares and
  returns 0, and one branch at the end. With contexts and a different frame:
…[4065 chars cut]…
am does from its statements, so a task a case, or a helper it
calls, spawns starts under the frame of its spawn; before, nothing a
suite reached was framed, and the task read nothing set.

A lambda's reads that its making sets are read there; the rest are owed
where it is called, since it runs laid over the frame it is called under.
A task's body still owes all it reads at its spawn, its only frame. The
design's capture rule says so.

use @std.meta.{derive}
use tree.prim.{prim}
use tree.view.{View}
use style.box.{Box}
use tree.sites.{Sighted}

@derive(View)
@prim(.Field)
export component field(@attr(.Label) label: string) {
    ..Box
    ..Sighted
    @attr(.Value) value: string? = null
    @attr(.Placeholder) placeholder: string = ""
    @attr(.Invalid) invalid: bool = false
    @attr(.Masked) masked: bool = false
    on input(typed: string)
}
//! `components/checkbox.av` — a binary choice whose label names it.
use @std.meta.{derive}
use tree.prim.{prim}
use tree.view.{View}
use style.box.{Box}
use tree.sites.{Sighted}

@derive(View)
@prim(.Checkbox)
export component checkbox(@attr(.Label) label: string) {
    ..Box
    ..Sighted
    @attr(.Checked) checked: bool? = null
    on change(checked: bool)
}
//! `components/dialog.av` — a modal layer; `label` names it, `open` is its

use tree.prim.{prim}
use tree.view.{View}
use style.box.{Box}
use tree.sites.{Sighted}

@derive(View)
@prim(.Dialog)
export component dialog(@attr(.Label) label: string) {
    ..Box
    ..Sighted
    @attr(.Open) open: bool = false
    @children items: List<dyn View> = []
    on dismiss
}

the studies above set the order.

## Authoring: decisions

Owner decisions of 2026-11-17, from the component authoring study. A component here is any
component (a queue, a command, a server), not only a UI one.

- **A component's own names are read through `self.`**, as today: head props, fields and
  state are `self.x`, and what stands outside the component is bare, so a reader tells the
  two apart at sight. Rejected: all bare (decided and withdrawn the same day; it hides which
  names are the component's); a leading dot, `.x` (it is the spelling of an enum variant,
  `shows: .All`).
- **A place is passed with no marker.** A seat declared `state` takes the caller's place:
  `stepper count`, `field "Name" { value: draft }`. Passing what is no place is a compile
  error at the call. Rejected: a call-site sigil (SwiftUI's `$x`, Svelte's `bind:`), since
  `state` fn parameters already take `stepper(c)` bare.
- **`state` stands in a component head**, as it does in a fn's parameters.
- **`state` always means a place** (owner 2026-11-18). A place is a `state` binding (local, module
  or seat) or a `state` field by any path (`self.draft`, `t.title`); a `state` field holds a Cell a
  copy of its record shares. A member `state x: T = d` given a place shares it; given nothing, the
  instance keeps its own. A value passed to `state` is a compile error, with no exception for a
  literal. A seed is an ordinary input the member's default reads once:

/// the marks written before it. `doc`/`annotations` read as `Fn`'s.

# The program layer's refusal suite

Each directory here is a package of its own, one case: a source the program layer must refuse
in the old path's words, or must build. `sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh` judges them all;
its head says what each file means. In short:

- `refuses.expected`: the old path's `avra check` words, its warnings aside, paths as `<case>`.
  Both the old `check` and `AVRA_PROGRAM=1 avra build` exit 1 saying exactly this.
- `prints.expected`: what the product prints. The old `check` exits 0, the program layer builds
  the package, and its binary prints exactly this.
- `differs.why`: the paths are known to differ here, for the reason on its first line. The case
  is said and not failed while it differs, and fails once it holds until the file goes.
  `sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh --known` lists them.

A new case is a directory with `avra.toml` and `src/main.av`; `PIN=1 sh
tools/witness_program_refusal.sh build/avra-try <case>` gives it the old path's expectation.

WHY HERE AND NOT UNDER A PACKAGE'S `src/`: `avra test` builds every package nested under a
package's sources as a suite of its own (`nested_roots` in compiler/suite.av), so a case that must
be refused would fail that package's tests. Under `tools/` no suite reaches them, as with
`tools/wasm-refuses/`.

ctx db: string

type Store = { n: int, opened: Cell<string> }

impl Store {
    fn run() -> string { "${self.lazy()}:${self.n}" }

    fn lazy() -> string {
        if self.opened.get() == "" { self.opened.set(ctx.db) }
        self.opened.get()
    }
}

type Home = { open: fn() -> string }

fn stored_with() -> Home { Home { open: () -> "home@${ctx.db}" } }

fn named_read() -> string { ctx.db }

fn helper_spawn() -> string {
    ctx db = "C"
    let t = spawn named_read()
    t.await
}

            let home = stored_with()
            ctx db = "B"
            let t = spawn (home.open)()
            t.await == "home@B"
        }
    }
    given "a set in a helper the case calls" {
        then "a named fn it spawns reads it" { helper_spawn() == "C" }
    }
}

//! `ctx` — a value the program declares once and any fn reads, set for a block by the code that
//! calls it: `ctx theme: Theme = plain()` declares one, `ctx theme = dark` sets it until its block
//! ends, `ctx.theme` reads it. The running task holds one frame of them, so a set reaches every read
//! made under it, through any call, and nothing else.
use features.{LanguageFeature}
// LICENSED modules.unused_import: `Fixed` and `Term` are named by GENERATED code, not by this
// file — a rule that states a payload writes a `Fixed` literal, and one that builds a node in
// place writes a `Term`. Resolve needs the names the source never spells.
use @std.grammar.{Grammar, Rule, Alt, Seq, Item, Prim, Rep, Build, Fixed, Term, Expect, Recover}
use diagnostics.{DiagCode}

export fn contexts() -> LanguageFeature {
    let codes = table<DiagCode> {
        kind           | summary
        "ctx.unknown"  | "`ctx.name` reads a context, and no `ctx name` is declared"
        "ctx.where"    | "a context is declared at a module's top level and set inside a body"
        "ctx.required" | "a required context is set before the program reads it"
        "ctx.unread"   | "a context's set is read by something it is in force over"
        "ctx.old_path" | "`ctx` is built on the program layer"
    }
    LanguageFeature contexts {
        gram: grammar {
            stmt = CTX name:NAME "=" value:expression END -> Stmt.CtxSet
            stmt = CTX name:NAME ":" ty:type ( "=" value:expression )? END -> Stmt.CtxDecl
            primary = CTX "." name:NAME -> Expr.CtxRead
        }
        diags: codes
    }
    contexts
}

fn class_worn(worn: Cell<List<int>>, kinds: List<int>, t: Token) -> int {
    let key = token_class(t)

    let bits = class_bits(avra_lexeme(), kinds, t)
    worn.set_at(key, bits)
    bits
}

The trap reproduces: `avra run` stops with "index 84 is out of bounds (length 84)". Now the fix: the table grows to whatever class it is asked, so a new token kind can't outrun it.

### 2026-11-19T14:43:48 RUN Bash [SPWn7U2R]
```
cd /work/avra && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='packages/std-avrac/src/grammar/bridge.av'
s=open(p).read()
old_a='''/// What each token class wears, by `token_class`: -1 until a token of it is asked.
export fn token_classes_worn() -> Cell<List<int>> {
    Cell.new([0 - 1 for _k in 0..84])
}'''
new_a='''/// What each token class wears, by `token_class`: -1 until a token of it is asked. It holds no
/// class until one is asked, and grows to the class asked, so a token kind added to the lexer is
/// never past its end.
export fn token_classes_worn() -> Cell<List<int>> { Cell.new([]) }'''
old_b='''    let key = token_class(t)
    let known = worn.get()[key]
    if known >= 0 { return known }
    let bits = class_bits(avra_lexeme(), kinds, t)
    worn.set_at(key, bits)
    bits'''
new_b='''    let key = token_class(t)
    let seen = worn.get()
    if key < seen.length && seen[key] >= 0 { return seen[key] }
    let bits = class_bits(avra_lexeme(), kinds, t)
    if key >= seen.length { worn.set([if k < seen.length { seen[k] } else { 0 - 1 } for k in 0..key + 1]) }
    worn.set_at(key, bits)
    bits'''
assert old_a in s and old_b in s
s=s.replace(old_a,new_a).replace(old_b,new_b)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

//! `avra parsers <package>` — the generated parser held to the grammar engine on every file of
//! a package: each file's untold run on both, every builder call they make compared in order,
//! and how long each took. Says each file they differ on and exits 1 if any.
use @std.cli.{CliResult, Runnable, command, option}
use @std.avrac.compiler.{avra, avra_untold, avra_builders, avra_lits, Language}
use @std.avrac.grammar.{Token, avra_lexeme, lex_source, avra_token_tables}
use @std.avrac.features.{LangNode, build_named, BlockWords}
use @std.avrac.core.{new_node_store, loc_span}
use @std.grammar.{Captured, RunOutcome, run_untold}
use @std.relation.engine.{list_cell}
use @std.errors.{Loc}
use @std.io.{list_dir, read_text}
use @std.path.{joined_path}
use @std.time.{now_ns}
use @std.text.{parse_int}
use @std.avrac.core.{flatten}

type ParsersCmd = {}

impl Runnable for ParsersCmd {
    fn run(args: CliResult) -> int {
        let lang = avra()
        if lang.untold == null {
            eprintln(
                "parsers: the generated parser is not this grammar's — `./avra grammar --untold` makes it",
            )
            return 1
        }
        let mutants = parse_int(args.option("mutants")) ?? 0
        let held = flatten(
            [held_file(lang, f, mutants) for f in av_files(joined_path(args.arg("file"), "src"))],
        )
        let wrong = [h for h in held if h.wrong != null]
        for h in wrong { println("differs: ${h.wrong!}") }
        let clean = [h for h in held if h.clean].length
        let engine_ms = held.fold(0, (acc, h) -> acc + h.engine_ns) / 1000000
        let generated_ms = held.fold(0, (acc, h) -> acc + h.generated_ns) / 1000000
        println(
            "parsers: ${held.length} files, ${clean} clean on both, ${wrong.length} differing; engine ${engine_ms} ms, generated ${generated_ms} ms",
        )
        if wrong.is_empty() { 0 } else { 1 }
    }
}

/// `kept` against a text that may have moved above it since; null where the stream no longer
/// has that token, or the place stood past its end.
export fn placed_in(text: string, kept: Anchored) -> Loc? { placed_among(tokens_of(text), kept) }

/// `kept` against the stream a text lexes to now.
export fn placed_among(tokens: List<Token>, kept: Anchored) -> Loc? {
    match kept {
        .NoToken -> null,
        .In(p) -> {
            if p.lo_token >= tokens.length || p.hi_token >= tokens.length { return null }
            if p.lo_token < 0 || p.hi_token < 0 { return null }
            let lo = tokens[p.lo_token].span
            let hi = tokens[p.hi_token].span
            if !in_token(lo, lo.lo + p.lo_at) || !in_token(hi, hi.lo + p.hi_at) { return null }
            Loc { file: null, lo: lo.lo + p.lo_at, hi: hi.lo + p.hi_at }
        },
    }
}

/// The words a file is lexed under: its sublanguages', the components it imports, and the
/// components its own module declares.
export type LexWords = { grammars: List<string>, components: List<string>, own: List<string> }

/// A text lexed as its parse lexes it — under the file's words, so a raw block's body is the
/// block's and never read as comments.
export fn lexed_under(text: string, words: LexWords, keywords: List<string>) -> LexResult {
    lex_blocks(text, words.grammars, words.components, words.own, keywords)
}

## Authoring: decisions

Owner decisions of 2026-11-17, from the component authoring study. A component here is any
component (a queue, a command, a server), not only a UI one.

- **A component's own names are read through `self.`**, as today: head props, fields and
  state are `self.x`, and what stands outside the component is bare, so a reader tells the
  two apart at sight. Rejected: all bare (decided and withdrawn the same day; it hides which
  names are the component's); a leading dot, `.x` (it is the spelling of an enum variant,
  `shows: .All`).
- **A place is passed with no marker.** A seat declared `state` takes the caller's place:
  `stepper count`, `field "Name" { value: draft }`. Passing what is no place is a compile
  error at the call. Rejected: a call-site sigil (SwiftUI's `$x`, Svelte's `bind:`), since
  `state` fn parameters already take `stepper(c)` bare.
- **`state` stands in a component head**, as it does in a fn's parameters.
- **`state` always means a place** (owner 2026-11-18). A place is a `state` binding (local, module
  or seat) or

- **A key is any comparable value**: `key: t.id`, not `key: "${t.id}"`.
- **`words` and `reads` leave every primitive**: the derive that needs them adds them.

fn mark_before(ts: List<Token>, i: int) -> int? {
    if i == 0 { return null }

}

cd /work/avra/packages/std-ui/src && cat > headless/tests/seated_test.av <<'EOF'
//! A control's place, by its law: given one it shares it, given none it keeps its own, seeded from
//! `initial`; its gesture writes the place before its handler hears it, and `shown`, where given, is
//! what it shows instead — told each paint, never written.
use @std.ui.components.{checkbox, column, dialog, field, text}
use @std.ui.headless.{headless}

spec "a control keeps its own place where it is given none" {
    given "a field" {
        then "what is typed stays through the next paint" {
            let page = headless(() -> field "Name")
            page.fill("Name", "ab") && page.text() == "field \"Name\" value=\"ab\" placeholder=\"\""
        }
        then "it starts from `initial`, read once" {
            let page = headless(() -> field "Name" { initial: "x" })
            let seeded = page.text() == "field \"Name\" value=\"x\" placeholder=\"\""
            seeded && page.fill("Name", "y") && page.text() == "field \"Name\" value=\"y\" placeholder=\"\""
        }
        then "its handler hears what was typed, after the place holds it" {
            let heard: Cell<string> = Cell.new("")
            let page = headless(() -> field "Name" { on input { typed -> heard.set(typed) } })
            page.fill("Name", "ab") && heard.get() == "ab"
        }
    }
    given "a checkbox and a dialog" {
        then "a tick stays ticked" {
            let page = headless(() -> checkbox "Agree")
            page.check("Agree", true) && page.text() == "checkbox \"Agree\" checked"
        }
        then "a dialog sent away stays shut" {
            let page = headless(() -> dialog "About" { initial: true })
            page.dismiss() && !page.dismiss()
        }
    }
}

spec "a control given a place shares it" {
    given "a `state` the test holds" {
        then "typing writes it, and every reader sees it" {
            state draft = ""
            let page = headless(
                () -> column {
                    field "Name" { value: draft }
                    text "draft ${draft}"
                },
            )
            page.fill("Name", "ab") && draft == "ab" && page.text().contains("text \"draft ab\"")
        }
        then "a write to it is what the field shows" {
            state draft = "x"
            let page = headless(() -> field "Name" { value: draft })
            draft = "z"
            page.repaint() && page.text() == "field \"Name\" value=\"z\" placeholder=\"\""
        }
    }
}

spec "a control given `shown` is held to it" {
    given "a field shown in upper case" {
        then "typing is heard, and the field shows what the program says" {
            let heard: Cell<string> = Cell.new("")
            let page = headless(
                () -> field "Name" {
                    shown: heard.get().to_upper()
                    on input { typed -> heard.set(typed) }
                },
            )
            page.fill("Name", "ab") && heard.get() == "ab" && page.text() == "field \"Name\" value=\"AB\" placeholder=\"\""
        }
        then "a checkbox the program holds unticked stays unticked" {
            let page = headless(() -> checkbox "Agree" { shown: false })
            page.check("Agree", true) && page.text() == "checkbox \"Agree\""
        }
    }
}
EOF

/// The field a task is typed into. THE DRAFT IS THIS INSTANCE'S: nothing

    state draft: string = ""
    row {

            value: self.draft

/// task goes.

    item {
        checkbox self.task.title {
            checked: self.task.done
            on change { checked -> mark(self.task, checked) }
            style: title_style(self.task.done)
        }
        button "Remove" {
            on press { remove(self.task) }
            style: sunk_style()
        }
    }

//! An app on a live page, by its law: a paint is one frame of what
//! changed, an echo runs the handler bound to who spoke, and nothing is
//! sent for a page that did not change.
use @std.ui.app.{plain, remounted}
use @std.ui.components.{button, column, field, text}
use @std.ui.realize.dom.live.{live}
use @std.ui.realize.tests.support.{named, seat_for, Event}
use @std.ui.realize.dom.page.{Paged, paged}
use @std.ui.realize.dom.patch.{Says}
use @std.ui.realize.dom.tests.support.{records}

/// The frames a host was sent, in order.
type Host = { frames: Cell<List<Bytes>> = Cell.new([]) }

/// A page showing a count and a button that raises it.
fn counting(count: Cell<int>, host: Host) -> Paged {
    paged(
        () -> column {
            text "${count.get()}"
            button "Raise" { on press { count.set(count.get() + 1) } }
        },
        plain,
        live(),
        (sent: Bytes) -> host.frames.push(sent),
    )
}

/// The host's echo of a press on the control named `name`.
fn press(on: Paged, name: string) -> bool {
    let who? = named(on.page, name).first() else { return false }
    on.heard(who.n, seat_for(.Press).number(), Says.Nothing.code(), 0, null)
}

/// A door that fails the turn after its action ran, while `failing` holds.
fn contained(act: fn() -> bool, failing: Cell<bool>) -> Result<bool, string> {
    let ran = act()
    if !failing.get() { return .Ok(ran) }
    .Err("boom")
}

lexer: a member's `state` opens after the marks written before it

`cfield` reads marks then `state` (`@attr(.Value) state value: string`), but `opens_state` claimed

std-ui: a field, a checkbox and a dialog keep a place, and are held to what is shown

Each control's value is a `state` member: given a place it shares it (`field "Name" { value:
draft }`), given none the instance first built where it stands is kept, seeded from `initial`; a
value handed it is refused, as any `state` seat refuses one. The control's gesture writes the
place before its handler hears it, so a handlerless field keeps what is typed. `shown: T?` is told
each paint and never written: the node shows `shown ?? value`, so headless, the terminal and the
DOM page (written back where it holds otherwise) are held to it, and the HTML a page is first
served carries it.

The derive reads three marks for it: `@seeds(value)` on the member the place starts from,
`@over(value)` on what is shown in its place, `@sets(value)` on the event that writes it
(`@sets(open, false)` for one that says nothing). A primitive's kept place stands as a
composition's does (`stood`, a `Kept` seat), its spread fields carried each paint. A kept place no
event sets is refused, in new words.

Callers that passed a value now pass `shown:` (the program's truth, unchanged behaviour); the
boards' redundant draft and dismiss handlers go. A field always names its value now, so the
screens that read `field "n" placeholder=""` read `value=""` too.

//! `components/switch.av` — an on/off control whose label names it. `checked` is its place: given

use @std.meta.{derive}

use tree.view.{View}
use style.box.{Box}

@derive(View)
@prim(.Switch)
export component switch(@attr(.Label) label: string) {
    ..Box
    ..Sighted
    @seeds(checked) initial: bool = false
    @attr(.Checked) state checked: bool = self.initial
    @over(checked) shown: bool? = null
    @sets(checked) on change(checked: bool)
}

/// Whether the expression `e` reads the instance it stands in (`self`).
export fn reads_self(store: SyntaxArena, e: ExprId?) -> bool {
    let at? = e else { return false }
    store.expr(at) is .Receiver || store.walked(at).any((k) -> reads_self(store, k))
}

/// The field `p` signed: a `state`, or a prop whose type compares by value, is a cell — its parent
/// writes it at every paint, and a change is what the component sees. An event's field holds its
/// handler.
fn field_seat(engine: QueryEngine, signing: Signing, p: Param) -> FieldSeat {
    let ty: SignedType? = if p.ty == null { holder_type(signing, p) } else { signing.signed(p.ty!) }
    FieldSeat {
        name: p.name.of,
        ty: ty,
        state: p.state || p.prop && ty != null && compares_by_value(engine, ty!),
    }
}

/// The type the field holding the handler of the event `p` declares has: the fn its handler is,
/// handed the seats the event says and answering nothing, absent until one is set. Absent for a
/// seat that says none, and for an event a seat of which isn't typed.
fn holder_type(signing: Signing, p: Param) -> SignedType? {
    let says? = p.says else { return null }
    if says.any(it.ty == null) { return null }
    headed_type(TypeHead.Function) with { seats: [SignedSeat { ty: signing.signed(s.ty!), mutable: false, settled: false } for s in says], answer: owned_type("void"), nulls: 1 }
}

/// Whether two values of `ty` compare by value: a number, a truth, text or bytes, an enum none of

/// Each entry of the literal `lit` for a member shown over a place, written beside a place handed
/// that place: what it shows would stand over what the caller already holds, so the two are one
/// setting too many.
fn overshown(mut cx: Checking, lit: StructLit, fields: List<FieldSeat>) {
    for at, f in lit.fields {
        let seat? = fields.find(it.name == f.of) else { continue }
        let over? = seat.over else { continue }
        let placed? = lit.fields.find_index(it.of == over) else { continue }
        if !fields.any(it.name == over && it.placed) { continue }
        if !cx.placed(cx.store.unnamed(lit.values[placed])) { continue }
        let v = lit.values[at]
        cx.unhanded(v, seat.ty ?? cx.free_type(), lit.name.of, at, "${f.of} ${over}", Unhanded.Overshown)
    }
}''')

A plain default can replace it if the derive accepts any member the place's default reads, so it is the one mark the plain declaration can do without. Lean: drop it.
- `@over(value)`, on `shown`: the derive draws the attribute as `shown ?? value`, which holds the page to what the program shows. Without it, the derive can only guess the overlay from the name `shown` or from "the one `T?` beside the place". Ruling (2)'s law, "the MARK's, general to any component", would have no word to read. Lean: keep.
- `@sets(value)` (`@sets(open, false)` on dialog), on the event: the derive always binds the gesture and writes the place before the caller's handler, so a handlerless field keeps what's typed. Without it, the rule is "the event saying the place's type writes it". That can't express dialog's `dismiss` (it says nothing and writes `false`), and it's ambiguous once a control has two value events (slider change and commit). Lean: keep.
(2c) branch avra-lane-ui-language-item2 @ ed6003f0 (switch included; the marks are in packages/std-ui/src/tree/view.av). The `@over` law is parked unbuilt at /work/asks-back/over_law.patch.

Settled in the design review of 2026-11-18 (the lane's design: `avra-lane-ui-language-ctx.md`):

- **The value is a frame on the task**: one entry per declared `ctx`; a set copies the frame, a read
  is one load. A caught trap puts the guard's frame back by one store.
- **A change repaints by structure.** What a set's value reads are structural reads of the
  composition holding the set, so a write repaints that subtree whole; an exact patch never shows a
  stale context value. A child repainting alone runs under the frame its instance was drawn under.
- **A handler on a node runs under the frame the node was drawn under**, as a view does; a plain
  closure or a fn value keeps the frame where it was made.
- **The required check is sound through `dyn` calls**: a `dyn T` call counts as reading every `ctx`
  any impl of `T` reads (relayed by the compiler lead as the owner's ruling; measured: no refusal
  added on std-ui or the board). It runs at entries; `explain` shows an exported fn's reads.
- **A cached fn reads only a `ctx` that compares by value**; its key adds each read's value. One
  holding fns or cells is refused inside a cached fn.
- **No implicit default**: `ctx x: T? = null` is written out. `theme`'s default is the target's own
  default theme. A `ctx` is imported by name and shares the top-level namespace.

Owed before it is built, each as a real program: a cache keyed by a fn's inputs counts its
context reads; "this fn reads `db`" computed lazily, so a deep edit does not ripple through every
caller; a trap caught by a guard restores the context (on wasm a caught trap runs no cleanup

### 2026-11-20T00:28:32 AGENT
I've started ctx step 4 (cached-fn keys), but I'm holding the build for the lead's choice of design.

The bug is real. A `@query` answer is keyed by its arguments only, so it outlives the context it read. The repro is at `/work/asks-back/ctx_query_stale`: under `ctx scale = 10`, `scaled(db, 2)` answers 2 instead of 20.

My first plan had a phase problem. The compiler only learns which contexts a fn reads after lowering, but `@query`'s derive runs before that, so it can't add those values to the key. The two ways left:
- **(c), my lean: record at runtime.** The query engine records each `ctx` read made inside a query body as a dependency, as it already does for Db reads. A kept answer then stands only while the context holds the same values. It's exact on every path and needs no derive change, but it needs a hook from the context read into the running query.
- **(a'): a syntax-level read set for derives.** The derive walks the body and the callees it resolves to. It's exact on direct calls but duplicates the compiler's own read survey.

The repro stays outside the test tree until the fix lands; a known-failing test would break the suite. Item 3 is still held until batch 58's head arrives, when I'll check `tab` against layer-commands' head-field rule.

//! The lowering rules of `ctx`: a read is what the frame in force holds, a set makes the next frame
//! until its scope ends (core/contexts_lowered.av). A declaration runs nothing where it stands: its
//! default is its own unit, built at its first read.
use core.{Lowering, Lowers, StmtLowers, ExprId, StmtId, Reg}
use core.stmt.{CtxDecl, CtxSet}
use core.expr.{CtxRead}

impl Lowers for CtxRead {
    fn lowered(mut cx: Lowering, e: ExprId) -> Reg {
        let c? = cx.context(self.name.of, e) else { return cx.unlowered(e) }
        cx.context_read(c, self.name.of)
    }
}

impl StmtLowers for CtxSet {
    fn stmt_lowered(mut cx: Lowering, s: StmtId) {
        let c? = cx.context(self.name.of, self.value) else { return cx.stmt_unlowered(s) }
        cx.context_set(c, cx.lowered_into(self.value, c.held), s)
    }
}

impl StmtLowers for CtxDecl {
    fn stmt_lowered(mut cx: Lowering, s: StmtId) {}
}

// A PACKED LIST holds its cells and no marks: `marks` is NULL. Only a

// WHAT A RUNNING QUERY HEARS OF CONTEXTS. A context read inside a query
// body is one of the answer's reads, as a Db read is: the answer stands
// while every context it read holds what it held. The running task's
// slot holds a stack of recordings, one per query open on it, each a
// list of triples — a context's key, how its value is told apart, and
// the word that tells it — and `avra_ctx_heard_now` is that stack, NULL
// where no query is open: the one word a context read tests. Every
// other cost is the cold path's, out of line.
void* avra_ctx_heard_now = NULL;

// How a context's value is told apart: by its one word (a number, a
// truth, a word enum), by its text, or not at all — an answer that read
// one of those is kept by no cell. A default read is told apart from
// every set, the default being the same value every time.
enum { CTX_WORD = 0, CTX_TEXT = 1, CTX_UNTOLD = 2, CTX_DEFAULT = 3 };

// What tells the value `cell` holds apart, as `kind` tells it.
static int64_t ctx_word(int64_t kind, void* cell) {
    if (!cell) return 0;
    int64_t v = ((AvraArray*)cell)->data[0];
    if (kind == CTX_TEXT) return v ? (int64_t)avra_text_hash((const char*)(uintptr_t)v) : 0;
    return v;
}

// The stack of recordings the running task holds, made where `make`.
static AvraArray* ctx_heard_stack(int make) {
    AvraArray* st = (AvraArray*)avra_task_local->slot[AVRA_SLOT_HEARD];
    if (st || !make) return st;
    st = (AvraArray*)avra_array_sized(2);
    avra_task_local->slot[AVRA_SLOT_HEARD] = st;
    return st;
}

// THE COLD PATH: a context read inside a query body, its key `key`, its
// value told apart as `kind`, the cell a set gave it or NULL for its
// default — filed on the innermost recording.
__attribute__((noinline, cold))
void avra_ctx_heard(int64_t key, int64_t kind, void* cell) {
    AvraArray* st = ctx_heard_stack(0);
    if (!st || st->len == 0) return;
    void* top = (void*)(uintptr_t)st->data[st->len - 1];
    int64_t k = cell ? kind : CTX_DEFAULT;
    avra_array_push(top, key);
    avra_array_push(top, k);
    avra_array_push(top, ctx_word(k, cell));
}

// A query body about to run: a recording opened over the ones open.
void avra_ctx_listen(void) {
    AvraArray* st = ctx_heard_stack(1);
    avra_array_push_owned(st, avra_array_sized(6));
    avra_ctx_heard_now = st;
}

// The body ran: its recording closed and answered, the caller's own; what
// it heard is heard by the query open around it too, which reads this
// one's answer.
void* avra_ctx_listened(void) {
    AvraArray* st = ctx_heard_stack(0);
    if (!st || st->len == 0) return avra_array_sized(0);
    st->len -= 1;
    AvraArray* heard = (AvraArray*)(uintptr_t)st->data[st->len];
    if (st->len > 0) {
        AvraArray* outer = (AvraArray*)(uintptr_t)st->data[st->len - 1];
        for (int64_t i = 0; i < heard->len; i++) avra_array_push(outer, heard->data[i]);
    } else {
        avra_ctx_heard_now = NULL;
    }
    return heard;
}

// Whether every context `heard` records holds now, in the frame in force,
// what it held when it was heard: an answer that read one told apart by
// nothing never does.
int64_t avra_ctx_holds(void* heard) {
    AvraArray* h = (AvraArray*)heard;
    if (!h) return 1;
    AvraArray* frame = (AvraArray*)avra_task_local->slot[AVRA_SLOT_CTX];

        if (!cell || ctx_word(kind, cell) != word) return 0;

static AvraArray* ctx_recording(AvraArray* st, int64_t at) {
    AvraArray* r = (AvraArray*)(uintptr_t)st->data[at];
    if (r) return r;
    r = (AvraArray*)avra_array_sized(6);
    st->data[at] = (int64_t)(uintptr_t)r;
    if (!avra_packed(st)) st->marks[at] |= MARK_OWNED;
    return r;
}

// THE COLD PATH: a context read inside a query body, its key `key`, its
// value told apart as `kind`, the cell a set gave it or NULL for its
// default — filed on the innermost recording, made at its first read.
__attribute__((noinline, cold))
void avra_ctx_heard(int64_t key, int64_t kind, void* cell) {
    AvraArray* st = ctx_heard_stack(0);
    if (!st || st->len == 0) return;
    AvraArray* top = ctx_recording(st, st->len - 1);
    int64_t k = cell ? kind : CTX_DEFAULT;
    avra_array_push(top, key);
    avra_array_push(top, k);
    avra_array_push(top, ctx_word(k, cell));
}

// A query body about to run: a recording opened over the ones open — an
// empty place, made into a list only where the body reads a context.
void avra_ctx_listen(void) {
    AvraArray* st = ctx_heard_stack(1);
    avra_array_push(st, 0);
    avra_ctx_heard_now = st;
}

// The body ran: its recording closed and answered, the caller's own, NULL
// where it heard nothing; what it heard is heard by the query open around
// it too, which reads this one's answer.
void* avra_ctx_listened(void) {
    AvraArray* st = ctx_heard_stack(0);
    if (!st || st->len == 0) return NULL;
    st->len -= 1;
    AvraArray* heard = (AvraArray*)(uintptr_t)st->data[st->len];
    st->data[st->len] = 0;
    if (!avra_packed(st)) st->marks[st->len] = 0;
    if (st->len > 0) {
        if (heard) {
            AvraArray* outer = ctx_recording(st, st->len - 1);
            for (int64_t i = 0; i < heard->len; i++) avra_array_push(outer, heard->data[i]);
        }
    } else {
        // No query is open on the task: its slot goes empty, so a switch back loads NULL.
        avra_task_local->slot[AVRA_SLOT_HEARD] = NULL;
        avra_rc_release(st);
        avra_ctx_heard_now = NULL;
    }
    return heard;
}

// A recording no cell keeps any longer, let go.
void avra_ctx_heard_drop(void* heard) { avra_rc_release(heard); }

fn flag_tests(ins: List<Ins>) -> FlagTests {
    mut counted = FlagTests { calls: 0, edges: 0 }
    for at in 0..ins.length {
        let tested? = flag_tested(ins, at) else { continue }
        counted = match tested {
            .Unwinding -> counted with { calls: counted.calls + 1 },
            .Tick -> counted with { edges: counted.edges + 1 },
            .Frame -> counted,
        }
    }
    counted
}

/// Two bodies' instructions with each test of the running task's flags that one holds where the other
/// holds none cut out of it, and how many were: the unwinding tests only this layer's or only the
/// workspace's held, and the ticks only one held.
type AgreedTests = { ours: List<Ins>, theirs: List<Ins>, cut: FlagCuts }

/// How many flag tests one side held alone.
type FlagCuts = { ours: int, theirs: int, edges: int }

impl FlagCuts {
    /// One more test of the flag `tested` cut, from this layer's side when `ours`.
    fn counted(tested: RtFlag, ours: bool) -> FlagCuts {
        match tested {
            .Unwinding -> if ours { self with { ours: self.ours + 1 } } else { self with { theirs: self.theirs + 1 } },
            .Tick -> self with { edges: self.edges + 1 },
            .Frame -> self,
        }
    }
}

// proves: a `@query` body's `ctx` read is one of its answer's reads, as a Db read is — the answer
// kept under one value of the context is never handed back under another, and is reused under a
// later set of the same value; a context of text is told by its text; a query reused inside another
// is heard by it, so the outer answer moves with the inner one's context; and a context its value
// cannot be told apart by (a nullable) keeps no answer — in both engines
use @std.relation.{query}
use @std.relation.db.{Db, new_db}

ctx scale: int = 1
ctx unit: string = "m"
ctx maybe: int? = null

once fn runs() -> Cell<int> { Cell.new(0) }

fn ran() {
    let r = runs()
    r.set(r.get() + 1)
}

@query
fn scaled(db: Db, n: int) -> int {
    ran()
    n * ctx.scale
}

@query
fn labelled(db: Db, n: int) -> string {
    ran()
    "${n}${ctx.unit}"
}

@query
fn outer(db: Db, n: int) -> int { scaled(db, n) + 1 }

@query
fn maybe_scaled(db: Db, n: int) -> int {
    ran()
    n * (ctx.maybe ?? 1)
}

fn under_ten(db: Db) -> int {
    ctx scale = 10
    scaled(db, 2)
}

fn label_in(db: Db, u: string) -> string {
    ctx unit = u
    labelled(db, 3)
}

fn outer_under(db: Db, s: int) -> int {
    ctx scale = s
    outer(db, 2)
}

let db = new_db()
println("plain ${scaled(db, 2)} runs ${runs().get()}")
println("under 10 ${under_ten(db)} runs ${runs().get()}")
println("under 10 again, a later set of the same value ${under_ten(db)} runs ${runs().get()}")
println("plain again ${scaled(db, 2)} runs ${runs().get()}")
println("labelled ${label_in(db, "km")} ${label_in(db, "km")} ${label_in(db, "cm")} runs ${runs().get()}")
println("outer ${outer_under(db, 3)} ${outer_under(db, 3)} ${outer_under(db, 4)}")
let before = runs().get()
let a = maybe_scaled(db, 2)
let b = maybe_scaled(db, 2)
println("a nullable keeps nothing: ${a} ${b} ran ${runs().get() - before}")
EOF

# spends longer resolving than the census spent counting.
symbols_at() {
    if command -v atos > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        xargs atos -o "$census" 2>/dev/null
    else
        xargs addr2line -f -e "$census" 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR % 2 == 1'
    fi

// A program of context reads and no query: two contexts read a million times each, under sets
// made and taken back as often.
ctx scale: int = 1
ctx unit: string = "m"

fn weighed(n: int) -> int { n * ctx.scale + ctx.unit.length }

fn under(n: int) -> int {
    ctx scale = n % 7 + 1
    weighed(n)
}

mut total = 0
for i in 0..1000000 {
    total = total + weighed(i) + under(i)
}
println("${total}")

cd /work/avra && git add -A docs/2026_11_16_UI.md packages/cli/src/commands/tapes.av packages/std-avrac/src packages/std-relation/src runtime && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
ctx step 4: a context a running query reads is one of its answer's reads

A `@query` answer was kept by its arguments alone, so one made under `ctx scale = 1` was handed
back under `ctx scale = 10`. A `ctx` read inside a running query body is now a dependency like a
Db read: the kernel's run opens a recording at `begin` and keeps what it heard on the cell as it
settles, and an answer is reused only while each context it heard holds what it held — by its word
(a number, a truth, a float's bits, a word enum's tag), by its text's hash, or, for a default, as no
set. A context told apart by no word (a nullable set, a record, a list) keeps no answer. A query
reused inside another is heard by it, so the outer answer moves with the inner one's context.

A read outside a query costs one load of the runtime's word and a test, as a loop's tick does; the
filing (`avra_ctx_heard`) is the cold path, out of line. The rows touch only the running task's own
state, so a query run at compile time may use them. Both engines hold it: the evaluator keeps the
recordings in a task's slot, or beside the machine while no task stands.

std-relation/src/tests/ctx_heard proves it in both engines; runtime/tests/ctx_frame_test holds the
runtime's half; the census of a program of four million context reads and no query is the same
count for count, and its time within run-to-run noise.

//! A task spawned by a library fn reads the context that fn set, under `avra test` as under `avra
//! run`: the case framing a spec case runs under starts the spawned task under the frame of its
//! spawn (services' smallest form). `avra_ran`, `scratch_dir` and `exit_is_zero` are the
//! neighbouring tests' own.
use @std.io.{make_dirs, write_text}
use @std.meta.{embed}
use @std.time.{stamp}

/// A library whose fn sets a context and spawns a reader of it.
const spawning_lib: string = embed("ctx_spawn/lib.txt")

/// A spec case calling it from another module.
const spawning_case: string = embed("ctx_spawn/spawned_test.txt")

/// What `avra test` says of the package, once.
once fn tested() -> string {
    let root = "${scratch_dir()}/ctx_spawn_${stamp()}"
    let _ = make_dirs("${root}/src/tests")
    let _ = write_text(
        "${root}/avra.toml",
        "[package]\nname = \"spawn_ctx\"\nversion = \"0.0.1\"\n\n[lib]\nname = \"spawn_ctx\"\npath = \"src/lib.av\"\n",
    )
    let _ = write_text("${root}/src/lib.av", spawning_lib)
    let _ = write_text("${root}/src/tests/spawned_test.av", spawning_case)
    match avra_ran(["test", root]) { .Ok(o) -> "${o.out.stdout}${o.out.stderr}", .Err(_) -> "the test did not run" }
}

spec "a spawned task reads its spawner's context under `avra test`" {
    given "a library fn that sets `n` and spawns a reader of it, called from a spec case" {
        then "the case passes" { tested().contains("1/1 tests passed") }
        then "and nothing traps for want of the context" { !tested().contains("is required") }
    }
}
EOF

# ctx step 3, part b: the walk ("placed, not written"), a ruling ask

## The fact
std-ui's generated composition does this:

    fn made() -> List<dyn View> { let made = gathered { <body> }; made.items }
    fn describe(at) { made_of(at, me.made(), self.key) }

The body's `ctx theme = …` is a statement inside `gathered { … }`, so it ends when that block ends.
That is before `made_of` → `each_described` → `v.describe(...)` draws any child. With step 3a alone, a
child therefore never sees its parent's set.

F1's own example settles what "placed" means. In `form_box { button "Save" { on press {
ctx.form.submit() } } }`, the button is BUILT by the caller (before form_box sets `form`) but PLACED by
form_box's body, as `self.body`, after the set. So the frame a child is drawn under is the one in force
at the statement of the parent's body that yields it into `gathered`: not where it was built, and not
where the walk later calls it. Sets can sit between placements (`text "a"; ctx theme = dark; text
"b"`), so it is per item.

The step 3b design (placed frames) already makes a set in the root composition reach every descendant's `describe`. What it doesn't settle is the realizer. Today it gets the theme by argument (`live.patches(root, theme)`, the stylesheet, `hydration`) and runs in the app's paint, outside the board's set. So, with no argument threading, the theme has to ride the drawn tree. That choice shapes every realizer, so it goes to the lead before I build it.

<to_controller>
step 5 started. One design point needs the UI lead before I touch realizers:
- What I'm building: std-ui gets `ctx theme: Theme = plain()`. App, mount and paged lose their `theme` seats. Realizers take no theme argument.
- The problem: the board sets `ctx theme` in its root composition, but realizers run in the app's paint, outside that set. Node styles are tokens (`.Surface`, …) that the realizer resolves through a theme, so the theme in force where nodes are drawn has to reach the realizer through the tree.
- Proposal: a primitive's `describe` stamps the theme in force onto its Node only where it differs from the theme its parent was drawn under, and the root always carries it. The cost is one ctx read and one compare per primitive, and a stamp only where a set changes it. Realizers read the root's theme for the page sheet, as today with one theme per page; a nested themed subtree (scoped classes) is left for later.
- Alternative: drop per-node stamps and keep only the root's, with the realizer reading `root.theme`. Simpler, but a subtree's `ctx theme = dark` would draw in the page's theme with no error.
- Lean: stamp where it differs, and realize only the root's for now.
Meanwhile I'm doing what doesn't depend on it: the theme declaration, the new_task and task row slice, the four owed ctx programs, and the paint baseline (allocations and time before).
</to_controller>

import re
def uses(s, name, line):
    rest=s.replace(line,'')
    return re.search(r'\b%s\b' % re.escape(name), rest) is not None
fixes={'app/app.av':['use style.theme.{Theme, default_theme}','use style.contrast.{legible}'],
       'app/shown.av':['use style.theme.{Theme}'],
       'web/web.av':['use style.theme.{Theme}'],
       'realize/dom/page.av':['use style.theme.{Theme}']}
for p,lines in fixes.items():
    s=open(p).read()
    for line in lines:
        if line not in s: print("absent",p,line); continue
        m=re.match(r'use ([\w.]+)\.\{(.*)\}',line)
        mod,names=m.group(1),[n.strip() for n in m.group(2).split(',')]
        keep=[n for n in names if uses(s,n,line)]
        new=('use %s.{%s}' % (mod,', '.join(keep))) if keep else ''
        s=s.replace(line+'\n', (new+'\n') if new else '',1)
        print(p, line, '->', new or '(dropped)')
    open(p,'w').write(s)

//! `tests/support/spoken.av` — a paint as text a test reads: each patch one
//! line, each element spelled by the path it stands at. Never the wire.
use realize.dom.live.{Live}
use realize.dom.patch.{Patch, Held, Says, diff}

/// What a paint of `root` on `page` says, as readable lines.
export fn spoken(page: Live, root: Node, theme: Theme) -> string {
    let stood = page.page.get()
    patch_text(page.patches(root), stood.concat(page.page.get()))
}

/// Each numbered element under `run` and the path it stands at: its
/// ancestors' seats, then its own.
fn paths(run: List<Element>, above: string?) -> List<Path> {
    [p for e in run for p in paths_of(e, above)]
}

type Path = { n: int, path: string }

fn paths_of(e: Element, above: string?) -> List<Path> {
    let here = under(above, readable(e.reads()))
    let own = [Path { n: e.id().n, path: here }]
    let el? = e.tagged() else { return own }
    own.concat(paths(el.kids, here))
}

/// The path each number stands at, across the pages given.

    mut at: Map<string, string> = {}
    for p in paths(pages, null) { at.set("${p.n}", p.path) }
    at
}

…[1679 chars cut]…
// Patches as readable lines, each element spelled by the path it stands
/// at on one of `pages` — the page before a paint and the page after.
fn patch_text(patches: List<Patch>, pages: List<Element>) -> string {
    let at = path_table(pages)
    [patch_line(p, at) for p in patches].join("\n")
}

/// A tree's first paint as readable lines: the page built from nothing,
/// its sheet left out.
export fn drawn_text(root: Node) -> string {
    let made = diff([], lowered(root), [], 0)
    patch_text(made.patches, made.page)
}

/// The elements under `e` that hear an event and are named `name`.
fn named_in(e: Element, name: string) -> List<NodeId> {
    let el? = e.tagged() else { return [] }
    let own: List<NodeId> = if !el.hears.is_empty() &&
        el.attrs.any(it.name == HtmlAttrName.AriaLabel && it.value == name) {
        [el.id]
    } else {
        []
    }
    own.concat([id for k in el.kids for id in named_in(k, name)])
}

export fn scoped_sheet(root: Node, page: Theme) -> string {
    let page_wears = worn_by(page)
    let chains = scope_chains(root, [])
    if !chains.any(it.any(worn_by(it) != page_wears)) { return "" }
    mut seen: List<string> = []

}

}

fn tag_parts(key: string, ps: List<Placed>) -> List<string> {

//! A subtree set to another theme inside its page's is drawn in that theme by
//! every realizer — never silently in the page's. Headless and the terminal
//! carry the nearest stamp down; the DOM and HTML scope the subtree by a class
//! its theme names, its variables set on that element and its look under the
//! chain of scopes it stands in.
use @std.ui.components.{column, text}
use @std.ui.env.{Env}
use @std.ui.headless.{headless}
use @std.ui.realize.dom.live.{live}
use @std.ui.realize.html.css.{theme_scope}
use @std.ui.realize.html.html.{render}
use @std.ui.style.theme.{Theme, default_theme, plain, theme}
use @std.ui.terminal.{terminal}
use @std.ui.tree.view.{tree_of}

fn night() -> Theme { default_theme with { mode: .Dark } }

/// Words drawn in `worn`, set where they stand, around what `inside` places.
component worn_here {
    worn: Theme = plain()
    words: string = ""
    ctx theme = self.worn
    text self.words
}

/// Back in the page's theme, inside the night.
component back_home {
    ctx theme = plain()
    text "back"
}

/// The night, around a subtree back in the page's theme.
component at_night {
    ctx theme = night()
    column {
        text "inside"
        back_home {}
    }
}

/// A page in the plain theme with the night inside it.
component nested_page {
    ctx theme = plain()
    column {
        text "outside"
        at_night {}
        text "after"
    }
}

/// A page in one theme only.
component one_theme {
    ctx theme = plain()
    column {
        text "outside"
        worn_here { words: "same" }
    }
}

fn mode_of(t: Theme?) -> string { t?.mode.word() ?? "none" }

fn html() -> string { render(tree_of(nested_page {}), Env {}) }

fn night_scope() -> string { theme_scope(night()) }

fn home_scope() -> string { theme_scope(plain()) }

spec "a subtree in another theme" {
    given "headless" {
        then "the subtree is drawn in its own theme" { mode_of(headless(() -> nested_page {}).theme_of("inside")) == "dark" }
        then "the page around it in the page's" { mode_of(headless(() -> nested_page {}).theme_of("outside")) == "system" }
        then "a sibling after it in the page's" { mode_of(headless(() -> nested_page {}).theme_of("after")) == "system" }
        then "a subtree back in the page's theme inside it in the page's" {
            mode_of(headless(() -> nested_page {}).theme_of("back")) == "system"
        }
    }
    given "a terminal" {
        then "the subtree is drawn in its own theme" { mode_of(terminal(() -> nested_page {}).theme_of("inside")) == "dark" }
        then "the page around it in the page's" { mode_of(terminal(() -> nested_page {}).theme_of("outside")) == "system" }
        then "a subtree back in the page's theme inside it in the page's" {
            mode_of(terminal(() -> nested_page {}).theme_of("back")) == "system"
        }
    }
    given "html" {
        then "the subtree wears its theme's scope" { html().contains("${night_scope()}\"") || html().contains("${night_scope()} ") }
        then "its variables are set on the scope, dark" { html().contains(".${night_scope()}{color-scheme:dark;") }
        then "the subtree back in the page's theme wears the page's scope, set again" {
            html().contains(".${home_scope()}{color-scheme:")
        }
        then "the look back home is under the chain, so the nearest scope is the most specific" {
            html().contains(".${night_scope()} .${home_scope()} ")
        }
        then "a page in one theme scopes nothing" { !render(tree_of(one_theme {}), Env {}).contains("th-") }
    }
    given "the dom" {
        then "the first paint scopes the subtree and sets its variables" {
            let first = live().paint_view(nested_page {})
            first.contains(night_scope()) && first.contains(".${night_scope()}{color-scheme:dark;")
        }
        then "a page in one theme scopes nothing" { !live().paint_view(one_theme {}).contains("th-") }
    }
}

#!/bin/sh
# The exact path's own tests, run natively under AVRA_EXACT=check: each program
# in std-ui's realize/dom/tests, and the board's programs under tools/ui-board,
# that has a `.check` file must print exactly
# that, which names how many turns the exact path answered and how many it
# declined. With the flag unset the same programs print their `.expected`
# (the path is off), so eval == native == expected holds for the suite as it is.
# usage: sh tools/exact-patches/check_tests.sh [avra-binary]
set -eu
# usage: paint_measure.sh <label> — builds the paint program with /work/avra's compiler, census and shipping, and times it
. /etc/profile.d/avra.sh; export AVRA_MEM_POOL_MB=12500
L=$1; P=/tmp/claude-0/s7/paint; O=/tmp/claude-0/s7/paint-$L.sum; : > $O
cd /work/avra
counted="-DAVRA_CENSUS -fno-omit-frame-pointer"
make --no-print-directory CFLAGS_avra_runtime="$counted" CFLAGS_avra_hot="$counted" build/libavra_runtime.a > /dev/null 2>&1
AVRA_FRAME_POINTERS=1 AVRA_CENSUS_TYPES=1 AVRA_INLINE_RUNTIME=0 AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE=release timeout 900 build/avra-try build $P > /tmp/claude-0/s7/b-$L.log 2>&1; echo "census build $?" >> $O
cp $P/src/main /tmp/claude-0/s7/paint-census-$L
AVRA_MEM_STATS=1 /tmp/claude-0/s7/paint-census-$L > /tmp/claude-0/s7/c-$L.out 2>&1
grep -E "^first|^rc:|^alloc: [0-9]" /tmp/claude-0/s7/c-$L.out >> $O
make --no-print-directory build/libavra_runtime.a > /dev/null 2>&1
AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE=release timeout 900 build/avra-try build $P > /dev/null 2>&1
cp $P/src/main /tmp/claude-0/s7/paint-ship-$L
best=999999999; for r in $(seq 1 15); do s=$(date +%s%N); /tmp/claude-0/s7/paint-ship-$L > /dev/null; e=$(date +%s%N); t=$(( (e-s)/1000 )); [ $t -lt $best ] && best=$t; done
echo "best of 15: $best us" >> $O
echo DONE >> $O

#!/bin/sh
# THE GATE, IN SLICES: every receipt a landing is held to, cut into slices that each run alone in a
# tree of their own, so N machines run N slices at once and the gate takes as long as its longest
# slice. A slice builds the compiler of HEAD itself when build/avra was built from anything else,
# runs every row on the program layer, the net off but where a row's claim is the net, empties the
# stores a cold row reads, bounds every command, keeps each row's words under build/gate/<slice>/, and
# ends with ONE line:
#   GATE <slice> <sha8> PASS|FAIL rows=<n> failed=<n> <seconds>s
# exiting 0 on PASS, 1 on FAIL.
#
#   sh tools/gate.sh list               each slice, one a line, with what it holds
#   sh tools/gate.sh <slice> [arg]      one slice; the idioms slices take the base sha their diff starts at
#   sh tools/gate.sh seed               build/gate/compiler-<sha8>.tar.gz: HEAD's compiler — ONE generation, built
#                                       here first where none of HEAD's stands — and every object a tree
#                                       links with; `pack` is its other name. Run it once; every slice
#                                       then starts from `unpack` and builds nothing.
#   sh tools/gate.sh unpack <file>      seeds this tree from a pack, and holds its stamp to HEAD's: a
#                                       seeded slice builds no compiler
#

8:    refused() { echo "gate: $(basename "$pack") $1 — not seeded" >&2; exit 1; }

//! The old path's word on `ctx`: each form refused where it stands, so a program that uses one is
//! the program layer's to check and build.
use core.{ExprId, StmtId, TypeId, Reg}
use core.stmt.{CtxDecl, CtxSet}
use core.expr.{CtxRead}
use features.{StmtSemantics, Meaning, ResolveCx, TypeCx, LowerCx}
use diagnostics.{Voice, said_as}
use @std.errors.{Loc}

impl StmtSemantics for CtxDecl {
    fn type_stmt(mut cx: TypeCx, s: StmtId) { let _ = refused_here(cx, cx.stmt_loc(s)) }
}

impl StmtSemantics for CtxSet {
    fn type_stmt(mut cx: TypeCx, s: StmtId) { let _ = refused_here(cx, cx.stmt_loc(s)) }
}

impl Meaning for CtxRead {
    fn resolve(mut cx: ResolveCx, e: ExprId) {}
    fn type_of(mut cx: TypeCx, e: ExprId) -> TypeId { refused_here(cx, cx.loc_of(e)) }
    fn lower(mut cx: LowerCx, e: ExprId) -> Reg { cx.lower_defect(e, "a `ctx` read the old path refused was lowered") }
}

/// A `ctx` form, refused at `at`.
fn refused_here(mut cx: TypeCx, at: Loc?) -> TypeId { cx.spoken(said_as("ctx.old_path", at, old_path_voice())) }

/// What the old path says of a `ctx` form.

        message: "`ctx` is checked and built by the program layer",
        label: "a context's form",

}

std-ui declares `ctx theme: Theme = plain()`. Nothing takes a theme by argument any more: `app`,
`mount`, `paged`, `render`, `hydration` and the live page's `paint*` lose their theme parameter, and
`Env` its theme field. A node carries the theme it was drawn in as a `Stamp` where its frame's entry
for `ctx theme` differs from the nearest one drawn above it — one pointer compare per primitive
(`@std.meta.ctx_entry`, lowered to the new `avra_ctx_entry` row), one stamp per set. The root is
always stamped.

Every realizer honors a nested stamp. Headless and the terminal carry the nearest stamp down and
answer `theme_of(words)`. The DOM and HTML draw the root's theme as the page's, and a nested one
under a class its theme names (`th-…`): its variables set on that element, which the cascade nests,
and its look under the chain of scopes it stands in, so the nearest scope is always the most
specific.

The board's `theme()` goes. `board_page` sets `ctx theme` once from `dark`, with Crisp as data.
tools/ui-board/flip flips `dark` by its control under AVRA_EXACT=check: every turn is held to the
full paint (answered 0, declined 4). realize/tests/nested_theme_test holds a subtree in another
theme, and one back in the page's inside it, on all four realizers.

rounds stay the fixed point they were, bounded by ROUNDS. The package-wide `contexts_declared`

static void* ctx_laid(void* under, AvraArray* over) {
    AvraArray* u = (AvraArray*)under;
    void* next = avra_array_sized((u ? u->len : 1) + (over ? over->len : 1));

    /// it: listeners and nothing built. When it does not, the page stays empty

    /// never diverge in silence.
    fn adopt(root: Node, theme: Theme, print: int) {

        let rules = distinct_rules(rules_of(root))
        let css = page_sheet_of(rules, drawn_as(root, theme))
        if print_of(run, css) != print {

        self.next.set(placed.next)
        self.rules.set(rules)
        self.worn.set(worn_by_page(drawn_as(root, theme)))

    }
    /// changed, and the listeners this module binds. The sheet is kept when
    /// this tree's classes write the same one, and sent again when they do not.
    fn take_over(left: Page, root: Node, theme: Theme) {
        self.page.set([unheard(e) for e in left.elements])
        self.next.set(left.next)
        let rules = distinct_rules(rules_of(root))
        if page_sheet_of(rules, drawn_as(root, theme)) != left.sheet { return }
        self.rules.set(rules)
        self.worn.set(worn_by_page(drawn_as(root, theme)))
        self.sheet.set(left.sheet)
    }
    fn restyled(root: Node, theme: Theme, notice: Node?) -> List<Patch> {

            self.rules.get().concat(rules_of(root)).concat(rules_of_notice(notice)),
        )

        if rules.length == self.rules.get().length && self.worn.get() == wears { return [] }
        self.rules.set(rules)
        self.worn.set(wears)
        let css = page_sheet_of(rules, drawn_as(root, theme))
        self.sheet.set(css)
        [Patch.Style(css)]
    }

/// The queue `name` of `ctx.db`, opened under `terms`.
fn opened<T>(
    name: string,
    terms: Terms,
    dedupe: Duration,
    wire: Wire<T>,
    sync: Sync,
    poll: Duration,
    clock: fn() -> Time,
) -> Result<Lasting<T>, HomeError> {
    let store = store_home_with<T>(ctx.db, name, terms, wire, sync, dedupe)? with { clock: clock }
    let heard = listening(store, poll)
    Lasting {
        home: heard.home() with { settles: Settles {
            run: (d: Delivery<T>, work: fn(Delivery<T>) -> bool) -> settled_on(store, d, work),
        } },
        send_as: (item: T, k: Key, id: string) -> heard.send_as(item, k, id),
        delay_as: (item: T, k: Key, id: string, after: Duration) -> heard.send_as_after(item, k, id, after),
        joins: (tx: dyn Transaction) -> heard.joins(tx),
    }
}

/// `store`'s settle with `ctx.db` set to its connection, so a handler
/// that reads the context writes inside the transaction it stands in.
fn settled_on<T>(store: Store<T>, d: Delivery<T>, work: fn(Delivery<T>) -> bool) -> Result<
    bool,
    HomeError,
> {
    ctx db = store.db
    store.settled_in(d, work)
}

fn answered(routes: List<Route>, line: string, token: string = "Bearer op") -> string {
    let q? = asked(line, token) else { return "unframed" }
    let r = dispatch(compiled(routes), q)
    "${r.status} ${r.body.text() ?? ""}"
}

/// A database with three orders, one of them buried in a letter.
fn stocked() -> Result<List<Route>, HomeError> {
    ctx db = homed(Db.memory())?
    queue<Order> orders {
        name: "orders"
        durable: stored<Order>(clock: ticking)
        retries: 1
    }
    queue<Dead<Order, string>> unpacked {
        name: "orders/dead"
        durable: stored_dead<Order>(clock: ticking)
    }
    worker packer {
        reads: orders
        each: packed
        dead: unpacked
    }
    let _ = orders.send(Order { sku: "nil", qty: 0 })?
    let _ = drain(packer)
    let _ = orders.send(Order { sku: "a1", qty: 2 })?
    let _ = orders.send(Order { sku: "b2", qty: 1 })?
    let _ = orders.home().take()?
    queue_admin(ctx.db, operator, ticking).found
}

/// What each line answers, one per line, with the database's mark cut
/// from every id so the answer does not depend on it.
/// A line heading `GUEST ` is asked with a token the guard refuses.

#!/bin/sh
# THE EXACT-COUNT GATE'S MEASUREMENT: the census compiler of this tree, run over FIXED workloads whose
# sources are one pinned commit (the `snapshot` row of tools/cost.baseline): cold, each run's census
# kept as build/cost/<workload>.out; and warm after each edit of a fixed set, the answers it worked out
# again kept as build/cost/edit-<kind>.out. tools/cost_ratchet.py judges them.
#   sh tools/cost.sh                      the baseline's snapshot
#   COST_SNAPSHOT=<sha> sh tools/cost.sh  another snapshot (what `make cost-accept` records)
#   COST_COMPILER=<file> sh tools/cost.sh a census compiler already built from this tree
#
# A FIXED INPUT MEASURES THE COMPILER: the snapshot is exported whole, std included, and the census
# compiler stands at its build/avra beside the objects a build links, so every package it reads is
# the snapshot's.
# ONE PROCESS ON ONE CORE DOES ALL THE WORK: a forked worker's counts are its own, so no body is
# lowered ahead (AVRA_WORK_AHEAD_OFF) and the run is held to one core (`taskset`), the width every
# emitter reads, so objects are made in this process by one worker.
# EVERY COLD RUN STARTS BARE: an empty store, and no product a run before it left, which a build reads.
# A FILE IS READ ONLY ONCE IT IS OLDER THAN THE STAMP WINDOW (io.stamp withholds a stamp from a path
# changed in the last two seconds), so what a run stamps never depends on how fast it began.
snapshot=${COST_SNAPSHOT:-$(awk '$1 == "snapshot" { print $2 }' tools/cost.baseline 2> /dev/null)}
[ -n "$snapshot" ] || { echo "cost: tools/cost.baseline names no snapshot"; exit 1; }
# A SHALLOW CLONE FETCHES THE ONE COMMIT IT PINS.
# The cold workloads: a name, the machine's store it runs over, then the command the census compiler
# runs in the snapshot. A STORE IS NOT THE COMPILER: every run but one has the machine's store off, so
# its rows are what the compiler does, whatever a store holds; `cold-with-store-fill` is the cli's
# cold check over an empty store, which it fills — the store's own price, ratcheted apart.

}
